metadataReview.note: The September 1941 attack is located at the town of Šabac, the German-held garrison town attacked by the insurgent detachments. The Znaci chronology records the attack launched at 23:00 on 21 September and a renewed attack on 22 September that reached the town centre before being driven back. The point is a town-scale reference, not a unit position. The existing start and end dates are retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred from these sources.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: OpenStreetMap place node 254036931 for the city of Šabac is published by Nominatim at latitude 44.7571535, longitude 19.6953972, rounded to [19.6954,44.7572]. GeoNames 3191376 places the same town about 1.2 km further south (44.74667, 19.69), so the point is a town-scale reference only. The Znaci chronology names Šabac itself as the objective and records insurgent units reaching the town centre on 22 September 1941. The point is not a German garrison position, an attackers’ line or the extent of the fighting, and it does not represent the surrounding Mačva villages. No accuracy radius is claimed.
